absent: Rescue budget accrual, admission and escalation policy beyond field roles.
Balancing, push and pull algorithms using cached priorities, deadlines, utilization and overload masks.
Runqueue clock update protocol and lock ordering beyond stated nesting.
No-hz, high-resolution tick, core-scheduling, bandwidth and statistics behavior.
Feature names and domain flag values from included headers.
State machines for enqueue, dequeue, wakeup and migration transitions.

findings.text: Rescue state for the extensible scheduler centers on a dispatch queue holding stranded tasks plus a nanosecond execution budget with its last accrual timestamp. It admits one rescued task at a time, recording the admitted slice and the runtime counter snapshot at admission. A timer paces admission and escalation, and a timestamp records the most recent ejection and must be set before any ejection occurs.

Per-CPU extensible runqueue state is built around a local dispatch queue with runnable and deferred-local lists and a running count. An optional sub-scheduler build adds a staging queue for capacity-rejected tasks and embedded rescue state. It preserves remote activation flags and scheduler across activation, tracks a capacity target, immediate-enqueue count, selection and release booleans and generic flags, counts dispatch-lock releases under core scheduling, maintains a per-queue clock, pending capability syncs and previous dispatch pointer, sync masks with pending kick state, IRQ-driven and balance-callback machinery for deferred requeue and CPU kicking, and a raw lock guarding deferred requeue lists.

Real-time per-CPU queue pairs a priority array with total and round-robin running counts, cached current and next highest priorities, an overload marker, a pushable list and a queued count. Group scheduling adds throttled state, consumed and allotted time, a runtime lock nested inside the runqueue lock, a boosted count and a back pointer to the top-level queue. Membership scheduling adds the owning task group for this CPU.

Deadline per-CPU queue uses a cached red-black tree ordered by deadline with a running count and cached current and next deadlines to guide migration decisions. It tracks overload, current entity, a cached tree of pushable tasks ordered by deadline, active utilization that rises on wakeup and falls on block, assigned utilization that follows task arrival and departure for inactive computation, extra and maximum reclaimable bandwidth, and an inverse reclaim fraction for the GRUB algorithm.
Performance domain node pairs an energy-model pointer with a next link and an RCU reclamation head for safe teardown.

Root domain aggregates reference and real-time overload counts with an RCU head, span and online masks, global overload and overutilization markers, a deadline-overload mask with its count, bandwidth control, a CPU deadline tracker and a monotonically increasing visit cookie used to detect whether bandwidth was checked.

The same root domain carries conditional real-time push machinery with an IRQ work item, a raw lock, in-lock loop cursors and lockless atomic progress markers, plus a real-time overload mask, a CPU priority tracker and an RCU-protected list of performance domains intersecting its CPUs.
Utilization clamp packs a value and task count into bitfields sized from capacity scale; the per-queue clamp holds one current value plus an array of such buckets.

Central per-CPU runqueue opens with a hot header intended for lockless reads holding running, NUMA-related, wakeup-pending and capacity data, scheduling and execution context pointers that alias when proxy execution is off, and the idle task. The next cache line holds an aligned switch count, the raw runqueue lock, no-hz state, cache-aligned clamp values with flags, class sub-queues for fair, real-time, deadline and optional extensible plus fair and deadline servers, and cache-epoch state.

The middle runqueue region tracks fair group leaf lists, NUMA migration state, cache locality counts, a global uninterruptible tally updated under lock, deadline server and stop task pointers, next-class selector, balance deadline and previous address space. It groups task, proportional and idle clocks with lost-idle time, update flags and 32-bit copies where needed, reschedule observations, barrier state, parent domain and topology pointers, balance callbacks, idle-balance bytes, misfit load, active-balance coordination with target CPU and stop work, identity and online state, a fair task list and averaged load for real-time, deadline, interrupt and hardware pressure with idle stamps and a cost bound.

The tail runqueue region covers hotplug waiting, interrupt and steal-time accounting, load-calculation state, high-resolution tick state, scheduling statistics for latency, yield, context switch and wakeup, RCU-guarded idle state, pinned and push-busy counts with push work, core-scheduling pointers, sequences, cookies and force-idle accounting, a scratch mask for use under lock, bandwidth signaling and an I/O-wait counter. Overall layout disables structure randomization.

Migration flag push equals 0x01. Presence marker for real-time push via IPI is defined when supported. Runqueue clock flags use 0x01 for requested skip, 0x02 for actual skip and 0x04 for updated. Idle clamp flag equals 0x01.
Accessor returns the calling CPU runqueue by dereferencing the per-CPU runqueues variable.
Raw locking helper saves interrupt state, acquires the raw runqueue lock and returns the saved flags for later restoration, annotated as acquiring the queue lock.
Runqueue pin context bundles saved interrupt flags, a pin cookie and a stashed copy of the updated clock bit so repinning can restore it.

Scoped guard constructors associate task-runqueue locking, plain runqueue locking, interrupt-disabling locking, interrupt-saving locking and raw interrupt-saving locking with automatic cleanup attributes.
Current-CPU locking helper disables interrupts, fetches the local runqueue, acquires its lock and returns the queue with an acquire-return annotation.
Topology enumeration orders direct, glueless mesh and backplane. Fault accounting enumeration orders memory, CPU and their buffered variants with memory at zero.
Domain flag helper scales an identifier by whether shared-child is set, and a shared-child mask constant aggregates the included flag definitions terminated by zero.

Capacity descriptor is reference counted and holds total, minimum and maximum per-CPU capacity, next update time, an imbalance scratch field, an identifier and a trailing balance mask. Scheduling group forms a circular list with reference count, weight, core count, capacity pointer, asymmetric preferred CPU, flags and a trailing CPU mask whose length depends on booted CPUs.
Fair group state bundles a fair queue, a scheduling entity and statistics and disables layout randomization.

Feature names expand into enumeration constants from an included list with a count sentinel, and separately into per-feature static-branch predicates that query the enabled or disabled state of a given key.

Wakeup cause bits use 0x02 for exec, 0x04 for fork and 0x08 for wakeup mapped to balance entry points, plus 0x10 for synchronous waker sleep, 0x20 internal migrated marker, 0x40 current-CPU preference and 0x80 selector-invoked marker.
Idle priority uses weight 3 with multiplier 1431655765.

Dequeue low bits use 0x01 sleep, 0x02 save, 0x04 move and 0x08 no-clock mirroring enqueue wakeup, restore, move and no-clock, plus 0x10 migrating, 0x20 delayed and 0x40 class mirroring enqueue counterparts. High bits use 0x10000 special and 0x20000 throttle.

Enqueue low bits use 0x01 wakeup, 0x02 restore, 0x04 move, 0x08 no-clock, 0x10 migrating, 0x20 delayed and 0x40 class. High bits use 0x10000 head, 0x20000 replenish, 0x40000 migrated, 0x80000 initial, 0x100000 runqueue-selected and 0x200000 queued. Retry sentinel is an all-bits-set pointer value.
Affinity change context carries a new mask pointer, a user mask pointer and flags.

Scheduling class interface starts with an optional clamp-enabled marker and queue operations for enqueue, dequeue with success result, voluntary yield, directed yield with success result and preemption check on wakeup.

The same interface provides load balancing with status result, task selection returning a task, previous and next task hand-off, CPU selection returning a CPU, runqueue migration on CPU change, woken notification, allowed-CPUs update, online and offline handling, locked-queue lookup for pushing, and periodic tick handling.

Remaining class operations cover fork, death without locks, transitions around a class change with priority query and change notification, reweighting, round-robin interval query, current-task update, optional group change and optional core-scheduling throttle check.

Queue and wakeup operations run under runqueue lock or task-runqueue lock depending on caller path, balance and selection under runqueue lock, CPU selection and fork under process lock, migration under process or runqueue lock, affinity change under task-runqueue lock with class-change context, online transitions under runqueue lock, push lookup under process plus runqueue locks, and tick and interval queries under the documented queue or task locks.

Registration macro defines an aligned class instance in a dedicated section. Active-class iterator advances past fair when the extensible scheduler has taken over all and past extensible when disabled. Range helper iterates a class pointer between bounds.
